user_problem: Offshore wind turbine blades accumulate ice in winter, cutting power output. The operator wants ice protection that survives salt spray and high winds.

mechanism_state.mechanism: Combined n-tetradecane phase-change microcapsule/polyurethane (PCMS-PUR) coating plus electrothermal heating induces interfacial softening and a lubricating meltwater layer in saline ice, causing whole-block sliding detachment rather than progressive melting.
mechanism_state.intervention: Coat offshore wind turbine blade leading edges with an n-tetradecane PCMS-PUR coating and embed electrothermal heaters operated at 8–12 kW/m² heat flux, so the phase-change buffering plus heating softens the saline ice interface under salt spray and high wind.
mechanism_state.expected_effect: Saline ice detaches as whole blocks via interfacial sliding, lowering de-icing energy demand and ice adhesion in cold marine environments, thereby restoring winter power output while the polyurethane matrix resists saline droplet exposure and wind loading.

architecture.mechanism: Combined n-tetradecane phase-change microcapsule/polyurethane (PCMS-PUR) coating plus electrothermal heating induces interfacial softening and a lubricating meltwater layer in saline ice, causing whole-block sliding detachment rather than progressive melting.
